title: Some order placements failing
summary: At 15:22 UTC a feature‑flag rollout (new_pricing_path 0%→20%) enabled a new pricing code path in orders‑service. Within a minute the new code (PricingPathV2.applyCollar) began throwing ArithmeticException: Non‑terminating decimal expansion for the flagged accounts, producing a sustained ~10× rise in 5xx errors (≈2% of all requests) while all downstream services remained healthy. The failure is deterministic for the rolled‑out subset, explaining why retries do not help those customers.

hypothesis.mechanism: Feature‑flag rollout enables new pricing implementation (PricingPathV2.applyCollar) which performs a division that can produce a non‑terminating decimal, throwing ArithmeticException for affected accounts and returning 5xx.
predictions: Disabling the flag returns error‑rate to baseline.
Re‑enabling after fix eliminates the exception.

hypothesis.mechanism: Market‑data returns bad or delayed prices causing order validation to fail.
predictions: Orders‑service latency to market‑data would increase.

hypothesis.mechanism: Reduced token refresh grace period causes auth failures for a subset of users, leading to order rejection.
predictions: Orders‑service would see auth‑related error codes.

hypothesis.mechanism: Database connection‑pool exhaustion or query slowdown causes order persistence failures.
predictions: Active connections would approach max, CPU would rise.

facts.statement: Orders‑service error‑rate jumped from baseline 0.20% to a window mean 1.31% (last minute 2.36%) – ≈10× increase.
At 15:22:07 UTC a feature‑flag change rolled new_pricing_path from 0% → 20% on orders‑service.

First ArithmeticException in orders‑service logs appears at 15:23:00.7 UTC – “Non‑terminating decimal expansion; no exact representable decimal result (at PricingPathV2.applyCollar)”. 272 occurrences until 15:44:58.
Exception stack points to PricingPathV2.applyCollar, a code path only exercised when new_pricing_path flag is enabled.
Market‑data‑service showed only a few vendor‑rate‑limit warnings (429) and its error‑rate stayed at baseline.
Postgres‑orders, redis‑cache, auth‑service metrics all remained at baseline; no saturation or error spikes.
Auth‑service config change (token refresh grace 120→90s) occurred at 15:05:40 UTC – well before error surge.
Dependency graph shows orders‑service calls market‑data‑service (hard, gRPC, 500 ms) and postgres‑orders (hard); both downstream services were healthy.

assumptions.statement: The feature flag new_pricing_path enables the PricingPathV2 code path for the rolled‑out accounts (≈20% of traffic).
assumptions.reason: Standard flag semantics; rollout percentage matches affected customer share.

assumptions.statement: The ArithmeticException is fatal for the request and surfaces as a 5xx to the caller (edge‑gateway → client).
assumptions.reason: Orders‑service logs show the exception at request handling level; no retry logic observed.

assumptions.statement: “Some customers cannot place orders; retrying does not help those customers” maps to deterministic failure for the flagged accounts.
assumptions.reason: Consistent failure for same subset aligns with flag‑based rollout.

gaps.scope: Edge‑gateway / client‑side logs showing 5xx mapping to the ArithmeticException
gaps.reason: Not queried; would close loop to user‑visible error.

gaps.scope: Exact rollout percentage vs observed failure rate to confirm 20% ≈ “some customers”
gaps.reason: Only flag rollout percentage known; actual affected traffic not measured.

gaps.scope: Source diff for PricingPathV2.applyCollar to see the exact arithmetic operation
gaps.reason: Source code not available via provided tools.

actions.description: Roll back / disable new_pricing_path flag (set rollout → 0%).
actions.rationale: Stops the faulty code path instantly; eliminates the 5xx surge.

actions.description: Deploy hot‑fix to guard decimal arithmetic in PricingPathV2.applyCollar (e.g., use BigDecimal with MathContext) and add unit test for collar calculation.
actions.rationale: Prevents recurrence when the flag is re‑enabled.

actions.description: Verify error‑rate returns to baseline (<0.3%) and order placement succeeds for all accounts.
Add automated canary analysis for feature‑flag rollouts, improve numeric‑precision testing, and document flag‑rollout procedure.

open_questions: What exact input values (price, collar ratio) trigger the non‑terminating decimal?
Why was the flag jumped directly to 20% instead of a gradual rollout?
Do any downstream services (portfolio‑service, notification‑service) observe side‑effects from the failed orders?
